verdict.line: You lose if you auto-trade or facecheck his poke before level 6; you win if you survive to Fury of the Sands and catch him with Disdain down.

brief.thesis: Urgot's kit outranges Nasus at every stage before 6 — Corrosive Charge hits from 800 range and Purge adds Echoing Flames damage on top of autos at 490, while Nasus's whole kit (Siphoning Strike at 255, Wither at 700, Spirit Fire at 650) requires him to walk in to do anything. Nasus can't win the poke war, so the lane is decided by whether he can stack Q safely on cannons and survive to level 6-11, where Fury of the Sands and a completed Trinity Force let him force fights Urgot can't out-range.

theirWindow.when: his Q and E (Disdain) are both up
theirWindow.what: Stay off minions he's zoning and don't contest trades — he can land Corrosive Charge, dash in with Disdain to hurl you out of position, and rack up Echoing Flames damage on the follow-up autos for free.

yourWindow.what: This is your all-in window since he has no way to disengage or re-position you. Wither (W) to cut his movement and attack speed, drop Spirit Fire (E) under him for the armor shred, and pop Fury of the Sands (R) to drain and finish.

start.why: Measured as the top start (47.8% WR, 70.6% pick) — the extra regen and poke-reduction passive are what let you stand in Q range long enough to stack Siphoning Strike against his autos and passive procs.

boots.why: 46.8% WR, 44.1% pick — flat reduces the physical damage from his autos, Purge, and Echoing Flames procs, which is where most of your lane damage is actually coming from.

core.why: Highest-sample core path (48.3% WR, 149 games) — the attack speed and burst proc are your best way to punish him when his E (Disdain) is down and you finally get to fight at melee range.
Armor plus the attack speed slow on nearby enemies directly cuts into the autoattack and Purge damage his whole kit is built around.
Stacks with Soul Eater lifesteal to out-sustain his poke damage once you're trading in melee range instead of getting kited.

situational.when: urgot is building lifesteal or leaning on autoattack damage to win extended trades
you need cheap early armor and antiheal against his poke before trinity force finishes
you want more ability haste and wave clear instead of trinity force's single-target proc

runes.keystoneWhy: The healing and movement speed proc off autos let you safely step in for Q last-hits and step back out of his 800-range Corrosive Charge and 490-range Purge zone without losing health you can't regen.

summoners.why: Flash + Teleport measures the highest win rate (49.3%) of the three common pairings — Flash closes the gap to land Wither before he can kite with autos and Q, and Teleport lets you reset top lane safely while you stack Q and still show up with a completed core for the level 6-11 all-in window.

playing.title: Farm Q, don't trade autos
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike's 255 range means you only stack it by last-hitting; his 800-range Q and Echoing Flames punish you for standing and auto-trading, so prioritize the Q stack over contesting every cannon.

playing.title: Respect Disdain's 475 range
playing.detail: When his E (Disdain, cooldown 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s) is up, don't stand in a straight line near the wave — he can dash in, shield, and hurl you out of position into a Purge burst.

playing.title: Watch his Purge cooldown scale
playing.detail: Purge's cooldown drops from 12s to as low as 0s by rank 5, so once he's maxed W he can spam it in extended fights — don't sit in his 490 range during a long trade past level 9.

playing.title: Hold Wither for the all-in
playing.detail: Wither (cooldown 15/14/13/12/11s, range 700) slows both his movement and attack speed — save it for when you commit with R rather than wasting it on a poke exchange you can't follow up.

playing.title: All-in only when his E is down
playing.detail: Disdain is his only way to disengage. Once it's on cooldown, flash in, Wither, and pop Fury of the Sands (cooldown 120s) to drain his health and close the fight.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire before you commit
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (650 range, 12s cooldown) strips armor on anyone standing in it — place it under him right before the all-in so your Q and autos hit harder.

playing.title: Don't overstay low on his R
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death (cooldown 100/85/70/70/70s, range 2500) executes champions below its health threshold from across the map — disengage once you're low even if you won the exchange.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled from measured games on the current patch; the trade timing, Disdain-cooldown all-in windows, and skill-order reasoning are my own tactical read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep some distance to avoid being hit with Urgot’s (P). Focus on farming and healing with [Q], while going in with [R] + Unsealend Spellbook when Urgot’s (E) is on cooldown to gain the upper hand.
